transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Evan Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Brooks (CTO, Oakridge), Samir Patel (Head of ML), Rita Gomez (IT Security)

SUMMARY (auto): Redwood demo of Model Catalog, Console walkthrough of filter + compatibility matrix. Discussed benchmarks (latency/throughput/cost), quantization options, dedicated vs hosted, and security (SOC2, KMS, VPC). Next: pricing, compatibility matrix, pilot benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Evan: Hey everyone, Evan Morales, thanks for joining. We're gonna show the model catalog and console flow, uh, focusing on selection for clinical summarization and triage use-cases. Priya will drive the demo.
[00:00:15] Priya: Hi all, thanks. quick agenda: 1) model catalog filters and compatibility matrix, 2) benchmark columns and what they mean, 3) demo selecting model variants and routing rules, 4) Q&A.
[00:00:30] Dr. Brooks: sounds good. for context, we have a mixed infra -- some workloads on-hosted, some on-prem in a VPC. our big ask is predictable p95 latency for 512 token summaries and strict audit logs.
[00:00:42] Samir: and cost—if we can get close to current costs that'd help us justify this. also, want to validate clinical accuracy, not just latency.
[00:00:50] Priya: absolutely. quick show of the catalog: here you can filter by task (summarization, classification, embedding), by model family, by supported quantizations (int8, q4_0-ish), and by hardware compatibility (A100, H100, CPU). note: some of the model names in the catalog are curations of open models—there's sometimes a mismatch in transcription - like Llama 2 -> llama two, etc.
[00:01:15] [00:01:20] Evan: we'll also show benchmarks we ran: p50/p95 latency, throughput (tokens/sec at different batch sizes), and cost per 1k tokens. these are measured on our reference workloads but we provide the raw benchmark sheet if you want to run on your prompts.
[00:01:35] Rita: for security, we need SOC 2 and audit logs and SAML SSO. do you provide KMS integration for key management?
[00:01:42] Priya: yes, SOC2 attestation is available for hosted; Private gives you control plane in your VPC with customer KMS/HSM integration. logs and audit trails are surfaced in the Console. note: some of the automatic transcribed docs say K V cash instead of KV cache, sorry for the verbatim.
[00:01:58] [00:02:10] Priya: demo - clicking model catalog. Here's a table view: columns include model name, family, tasks, seq length, p50 latency @ 256 tokens, p95 latency @ 512 tokens, throughput @ batch 8 and batch 32, cost per 1k tokens, and notes about quantization friendliness.
[00:02:30] Samir: can you show an example: we care about 512-token clinical summaries. what would be recommended?
[00:02:38] Priya: sure - filter task -> summarization, seq length >= 512. we see a 7B open model (redwood-llm/open-7b) that's int8 friendly; p95 on A100 reference is ~220ms for 256 tokens, and ~420ms for 512 tokens in our sheet — that's p95 on hosted reference config. there's also an 13B q4 variant with higher accuracy but p95 ~800-900ms.
[00:03:00] [00:03:05] Dr. Brooks: hmm so the 7B is faster but we need clinical accuracy. do you provide evals or small clinical benchmark runs?
[00:03:12] Priya: yes, we support model-evals tied to your prompt sets. we can run a regression test and quality monitor; Redwood Optimize will track metric drift and flag regressions. also we can recommend quantization profiles that tend to preserve accuracy.
[00:03:28] Evan: also worth noting runtime features like KV caching and prefix caching for repeated prompts (e.g., templated HPI summaries) which can dramatically reduce p95 for sessions that reuse context. sometimes transcriptions show K V cash, which is weird but it's KV cache.
[00:03:45] Samir: what about throughput if we batch? our ingestion pipeline might have bursts.
[00:03:50] Priya: batching is automatic up to latency SLOs; in the catalog we show tokens/sec at batch 8 and 32. for example that 7B model scales from 1.2k tokens/sec at batch 8 to 3.8k tokens/sec at batch 32 on a single A100 reference. dedicated pools can be tuned with autoscale for bursts.
[00:04:08] [00:04:20] Rita: for Private deployment, is network traffic ever routed through Redwood? we need private-only egress.
[00:04:26] Priya: for Private, control plane is optional; you can run inference fully in your VPC or on-prem. nothing leaves your network unless you opt into telemetry; KMS is customer-owned. we can show architecture diagrams in the security pack.
[00:04:40] Dr. Brooks: and latency — if we run private on H100s, will we see better p95?
[00:04:46] Priya: yes hardware helps; H100 gives better throughput and lower p95 for large seq lengths, but it's also depending on kernel selection. our runtime picks kernels based on seq distribution and model architecture. again we can run a short bench on your H100 nodes to confirm.
[00:05:05] [00:05:20] Evan: walking through compatibility matrix: each model row has an entry "Compatible hardware" and a separate column for "Quantization support". for example open-7b: A100/H100/CPU (int8 experimental), q4_0 recommended on A100. Some names might be slightly off in the transcript, like 'q four zero' rather than 'q4_0'.
[00:05:40] Samir: can you export that compatibility matrix? we need a small spreadsheet for our infra team.
[00:05:46] Priya: yes export to CSV; we'll attach the raw benchmark spreadsheet as well - includes the run configs and raw results.
[00:05:55] [00:06:10] Priya: next, the Console: per-route dashboards, cost per model, token-level breakdowns, and ability to pin a model version to a route or define rollouts (canary/A-B). you can also set routing policy: latency-first, cost-first, region-first.
[00:06:25] Dr. Brooks: we like the idea of canary before global rollout. can the rollout fallback to a higher-latency but more accurate model if the canary fails?
[00:06:33] Priya: yes, you can define fallbacks to compatible model variants; policy can be failover-based or percentage-based. we'll note that fallback compatibility requires same output shape/contract for tooling.
[00:06:45] [00:07:05] Rita: auditing—are there immutable logs for each request? we need per-request metadata for compliance.
[00:07:12] Evan: yes per-request audit logs, with retention controls in Private; hosted also provides logs with configurable retention. logs include model version, latency, tokens, route.
[00:07:25] Samir: about cost—do the benchmark cost numbers include caching effects?
[00:07:30] Priya: benchmark sheet shows cold-run numbers without prefix caching; we then provide modeled cost curves with cache hit assumptions. for real workloads you should run the pilot to capture your prefix reuse patterns.
[00:07:45] [00:08:00] Priya: switching to model selection UX—search by prompt emulation: drop sample text to see recommended models and predicted latencies/estimated cost. here's an example: paste a clinical note -> recommendations show open-7b-int8 (fast), open-13b-q4 (higher quality), and a distilled 3B for very low-cost summary.
[00:08:20] Dr. Brooks: we care about hallucinations. do you have guardrails or tools for hallucination detection?
[00:08:28] Priya: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitors and evals hooks; you can run regression suites and set alerts. it also supports tool-calling patterns for retrieval-augmented outputs which reduces hallucination risk.
[00:08:40] [00:09:00] Samir: about model naming—some of our legal folks want licensed models only. how do you surface license/usage terms in catalog?
[00:09:06] Priya: each model row includes license metadata and a link to the model card; we can filter to only permissive licensed models.
[00:09:18] Rita: encryption at rest for logs and models?
[00:09:22] Evan: yes, encryption at rest; for Private you can provide KMS keys. hosted uses our managed keys with SOC2 controls but we can arrange key escrow via enterprise contract.
[00:09:32] [00:10:00] Priya: demoing the benchmark detail page: here's raw latency distribution histogram, p50/p95/p99 numbers; you can change token size to re-run estimates. note, transcription sometimes swaps p95/p99 in these exports, so watch the raw sheet.
[00:10:18] Dr. Brooks: could you walk through a canary config for patient triage route?
[00:10:25] Priya: sure. Route config: default model = open-7b-int8, canary = open-13b-q4 labeled 'higher-quality'. Canary at 5% for 24 hours, monitor accuracy metric (we provide eval hooks), fallback to default if error rate / latency threshold exceeded.
[00:10:45] Samir: and how do you integrate with our metrics stack? we use Prometheus and Datadog.
[00:10:51] Priya: we surface metrics via Prometheus endpoints and can forward traces to Datadog; also built-in traces in Console for request-level analysis.
[00:11:05] [00:11:20] Evan: talk about private pilot: typical flow is 1) exchange security docs, 2) share infra specs, 3) Redwood runs a 1-week benchmark with your prompt set on selected GPUs, 4) review results and tune.
[00:11:34] Rita: timeline for SOC 2 docs and contracts?
[00:11:38] Evan: we can send SOC2 and network diagrams today. contracting timeline depends on procurement but typical 2–4 weeks for enterprise paperwork.
[00:11:50] [00:12:10] Priya: demoing the export—click "export bench" -> CSV includes run command, docker image, seed, prompt set. we also include notes on kernel selection and quantization flags used.
[00:12:25] Samir: we might push for a dedicated pool if the numbers look good—can Redwood guarantee dedicated throughput?
[00:12:32] Evan: Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools with SLA-backed throughput and latency targets; autoscale policies and burst capacity available. we can size the pool during the pilot.
[00:12:45] [00:13:10] Dr. Brooks: anything about embedding models and vector search for retrieval?
[00:13:16] Priya: yes catalog includes embedding models and their throughput and cost numbers. Optimize recommends model family by query-per-second and vector quality. we support reranking flow as well.
[00:13:30] [00:13:50] Rita: data residency—can we keep everything in us-east-1?
[00:13:55] Evan: yes, hosted has region pinning; Private obviously inside your region. we'll note region in export.
[00:14:10] Priya: okay, quick deep-dive on quantization: some models are q4_0 friendly and maintain accuracy, others lose sharpness. we annotate catalog rows with recommended quantization and confidence notes from our applied ML team.
[00:14:28] Samir: how reproducible are the benchmarks? we need to run them ourselves on our infra.
[00:14:34] Priya: fully reproducible—benchmarks include the full command, docker image, environment variables, and seed. we also provide the harness.
[00:14:46] [00:15:00] Evan: let's go through a concrete example - pick model open-7b-int8 and run estimated cost for 10k 512-token summaries per day. the console calculator shows ~$X (model cost + infra + caching assumptions) — exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[00:15:20] Dr. Brooks: we will want to see both cold-run and warm-run costs; caching will matter a lot for triage templates.
[00:15:28] Priya: agreed. we'll include modeled cost with 0%, 50%, 80% cache hit rates.
[00:15:40] [00:16:00] Samir: for pilot, can we get a raw benchmark on our H100s with our prompts?
[00:16:06] Evan: yes, pilot on your H100s is part of the plan. we'll coordinate with infra and security.
[00:16:18] Rita: procurement question - does Redwood support Marketplace pricing?
[00:16:23] Evan: yes we have some cloud marketplace options; enterprise contracts are separate.
[00:16:30] [00:16:40] Priya: another caveat—some open models have license or export restrictions; catalog flags these. also, model accuracy varies per prompt domain; that's why we recommend small eval runs.
[00:16:55] Dr. Brooks: ok that's fair. any limitations around max sequence length? we often send 1,200 token concatenated notes.
[00:17:02] Priya: max seq supported varies; some models in catalog support up to 2048, some 4096. console filter lets you pick min seq length. we also support chunking strategies and streaming to handle large inputs.
[00:17:18] [00:17:40] Samir: concerning fallback routing—if the primary model is unavailable for a moment, will the system re-route mid-request or only at request boundaries?
[00:17:47] Priya: routing is per request; KV cache is per session so mid-request reroute isn't typical. fallback occurs at new request boundaries or on errors.
[00:18:00] [00:18:30] Evan: circling back to audit/security: we will send the security pack which includes SOC2, data flow diagrams, and details on KMS integrations and SAML SSO.
[00:18:40] Rita: great. share that please.
[00:18:45] Priya: quick note—sometimes transcripts flip names; if anything looks off in the meeting export we'll correct in the notes.
[00:19:00] [00:19:20] Priya: demo wrap - we'll attach the CSV exports of the compatibility matrix and raw benchmark sheet. you can then pick the top 2 candidates for the pilot.
[00:19:35] Samir: we usually prefer start with a smaller model to validate pipeline; then scale to a higher-quality 13B if accuracy needs it.
[00:19:44] Evan: makes sense. our recommended path typically: run quick eval on your prompts with 2 models (fast 7B int8 + 13B q4), examine accuracy/cost/latency, then do a 1-week pilot on dedicated infra.
[00:19:58] [00:20:10] Dr. Brooks: timeline — we need decision by end of Q1, so a December pilot would be ideal to inform budget.
[00:20:18] Evan: ok we'll prioritize.
[00:20:25] [00:20:40] Priya: any more technical questions?
[00:20:45] Samir: kernel selection—how automatic? do you let us pin kernels?
[00:20:50] Priya: runtime selects kernels automatically but you can override for private/dedicated with knob to pin specific kernel version. we document supported kernel options in the export.
[00:21:05] [00:21:25] Rita: last question - do you support data egress logs for auditors?
[00:21:32] Evan: yes, we provide per-request metadata and can export logs for audits. retention controls configurable.
[00:21:40] [00:22:00] Priya: ok recap: 1) We'll share pricing & SKU (Evan), 2) We'll share compatibility matrix + raw benchmark sheet (Priya), 3) Oakridge will provide prompt set and logs (Samir), 4) schedule pilot on H100 (TBD).
[00:22:15] Dr. Brooks: that captures it. thanks both.
[00:22:20] Evan: thanks everyone, follow-up items will come in email.
[00:22:25] [00:22:30] END OF CALL - actual audio had filler and occasional crosstalk.

Notes: exported attachments to follow: security_pack.pdf (SOC2, network diagrams), model_compatibility_matrix.csv, benchmark_raw_results.xlsx, pricing_sku.pdf.

Meeting recap (manual): Redwood showed Model Catalog filters, compatibility/quantization annotations, benchmark metrics and Console rollout/fallbacks. Customer requests pilot on H100s and prompt set for quality assessment. Redwood to send pricing and security docs within 48 hours.
